localFindings.description: The core mint loop `for (uint256 i; i < count; ++i) nftMinter.mint(dispatcherIndex, recipient);` iterates `count` times where `count` is an unbounded caller-supplied uint256. The only validation is `count != 0` (BatchMint__ZeroCount). There is NO upper cap on `count`. Each iteration performs an external CALL into the trusted tokenMinter (token transfer + ERC1155 mint + dispatcher price ramp), so per-iteration gas is substantial. A caller may pass a `count` large enough to exceed the block gas limit, reverting the whole batch, or simply forcing self-DoS / wasted gas. This is the structural locus of the reported live exploit: the function trusts a numeric `count`/`paymentAmount` pair supplied by the caller with no relation enforced between them other than the dispatcher reverting when funds run out.
localFindings.recommendation: Introduce an owner-settable maxBatchSize cap and require(count <= maxBatchSize). Note: the inner mint reverting on insufficient paymentAmount provides economic backstop but NOT a gas/DoS bound.

localFindings.description: batchMint accepts FIVE independent scalar parameters (paymentToken, dispatcherIndex, count, recipient, paymentAmount). There are NO arrays in the current signature, so there is no array-length cross-check to perform. The historical exploit narrative ('attacker could supply too many params') maps onto the unbounded `count` (LOCAL-001) and the previously caller-supplied minter argument (see dev NatSpec lines 18-29) which has since been pinned to owner-set `tokenMinter`. Confirm with the audit team whether the in-scope deployed bytecode matches this source: if an earlier ABI took a minter address or arrays, the live exploit surface differs from this source.
localFindings.recommendation: Confirm deployed ABI == this source. Document the removed minter parameter as a fixed historical issue, not a current one.

localFindings.description: Refund gate uses `if (remaining / DUST_THRESHOLD != 0)` rather than `remaining >= DUST_THRESHOLD`. These are equivalent for the refund decision (integer division is non-zero iff remaining >= 1e6), so behaviour is correct but the idiom is non-obvious. `totalPaid` accounting: when a refund occurs, `totalPaid = paymentAmount > remaining ? paymentAmount - remaining : 0`. Because `remaining` is the FULL post-loop balance (which can include pre-existing donations or nudge leftovers, not just unused budget), `remaining` may exceed `paymentAmount`, yielding a reported `totalPaid == 0` even though real spend occurred. The return value is advisory only and not used for any on-chain accounting, so impact is informational.
localFindings.recommendation: Document that totalPaid is a best-effort figure and can be skewed by donated/residual balances; off-chain consumers must not treat it as authoritative.

localFindings.description: Nudge payout transfers the contract's ENTIRE balanceOf(nudgePaymentToken) to `recipient` whenever count >= nudgeSize. The amount is read live from balanceOf, not tracked. Combined with the unbounded `count` (LOCAL-001), the cheapest path to clear the nudge gate is to pass a large `count` of genuine paid mints. The dev NatSpec argues pinning the minter forces genuine payment; that reasoning is cross-contract (depends on tokenMinter actually charging) and is DEFERRED to interaction analysis. Locally note: the dust refund at line 228 reads paymentToken balance AFTER the nudge transfer — if nudgePaymentToken == paymentToken the nudge would drain funds slated for refund, which is exactly why the line 200 up-front guard forbids that equality.
localFindings.recommendation: Defer nudge-economic exploitability to econ-scanner; the local guard (nudge != payment token) is verified present and correct.

externalEntryPoints.function: batchMint(IERC20 paymentToken, uint256 dispatcherIndex, uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount)
stateChanges: transient ERC20 allowance on tokenMinter (set max then 0)
validations: nudgePaymentToken == 0 OR nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken -> else BatchMint__NudgeTokenMatchesPaymentToken
NO check that paymentAmount relates to count * price (dispatcher reverts if short)

externalEntryPoints.function: rescueERC20(IERC20 token, address to, uint256 amount)

externalCalls.target: ITokenMinterV2 tokenMinter (owner-pinned state, NOT a param)
externalCalls.notes: mint() overload WITHOUT extraData. Pulls payment from this contract's max-approved allowance, mints ERC1155 to recipient, ramps dispatcher price. Reverts (rolling back whole batch) if paymentAmount allowance/balance insufficient or paymentToken mismatches dispatcher prime token.

externalCalls.trustLevel: semi-trusted (assumed standard ERC20; caller picks address)
externalCalls.notes: Caller chooses the token address. Assumes no fee-on-transfer (else upfront pull leaves less than paymentAmount and refund math skews). Per project known-issues, weird/FoT ERC20s are out of scope except USDT.
Full balance swept to recipient when count >= nudgeSize. Funded externally (yield funnel).

batchMintDeepProfile.signature: batchMint(IERC20 paymentToken, uint256 dispatcherIndex, uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount) external whenNotPaused returns (uint256 totalPaid)

parameters.paymentToken: IERC20 — caller-supplied token used to pay each mint. Address fully attacker-controlled. Used for transferFrom, forceApprove, balanceOf, transfer.
parameters.dispatcherIndex: uint256 — caller-supplied dispatcher route on the pinned minter. NOT validated against any allowlist locally; validity enforced by tokenMinter.mint reverting on bad index.
parameters.count: uint256 — caller-supplied number of mint iterations. Validated only as != 0. NO UPPER BOUND. This is the loop bound.
parameters.recipient: address — caller-supplied ERC1155 + nudge recipient. Validated != address(0).
parameters.paymentAmount: uint256 — caller-supplied aggregate budget pulled upfront. NO arithmetic relation to count enforced in this contract; only the inner mint reverting on insufficient allowance/balance ties them together.

batchMintDeepProfile.arrays: NONE. The current ABI has zero array parameters, therefore NO array-length validation and NO cross-array length check exists or is needed. Any 'mismatched array length' framing of the live exploit does not apply to THIS source; the live issue maps to unbounded `count` and/or a removed caller-supplied minter param (see dev NatSpec).
batchMintDeepProfile.loopBound: count (uint256, unvalidated max). Loop at line 207-209.
batchMintDeepProfile.perIterationWork: Exactly one external call tokenMinter.mint(dispatcherIndex, recipient). No per-iteration storage writes in this contract; all gas variance is inside the trusted minter (ERC20 pull, ERC1155 mint, dispatcher price ramp/storage write).
batchMintDeepProfile.gasCharacteristics: Linear in count with a heavy per-iteration constant (cross-contract mint). With no cap, large count can exceed block gas limit (transaction reverts, whole batch atomic). Attacker self-DoS / griefing of own tx; no partial state persists because allowance is opened before and closed after the loop in the same tx.
executionOrder: 5. load nudgePaymentToken; if set && == paymentToken -> revert (BEFORE any funds move)
10. if nudgeSize != 0 && count >= nudgeSize && nudgePaymentToken != 0: transfer full nudge balance to recipient, emit NudgePaid
11. remaining = paymentToken.balanceOf(this); if remaining/DUST_THRESHOLD != 0 refund remaining to msg.sender; compute totalPaid
batchMintDeepProfile.atomicity: Fully atomic: any inner mint revert (bad index, insufficient budget, paymentToken != dispatcher prime token, gas exhaustion) rolls back the entire batch including the upfront pull and any allowance change.

trustAssumptions: tokenMinter is owner-configured and honest; it genuinely charges paymentToken per mint (the anti-drain argument depends on this — cross-contract, deferred).
paymentToken is a standard non-fee-on-transfer ERC20 (FoT/weird tokens out of scope per project known-issues except USDT).
nudgePaymentToken is owner-configured and funded externally; the owner can also drain it via rescueERC20 / nudge setters (centralization acknowledged).
pauser (global Pauser) is trusted to pause/unpause batchMint.
Owner is trusted (can set minter, nudge knobs, rescue any ERC20).
